input.summary:
Implemented a complete Task Management REST API in TypeScript with the following components:

**Files Created (8 source files):**
- `src/types.ts` — All shared interfaces and type contracts (User, Project, Task, Comment, Notification, all IService interfaces, event payload types)
- `src/event-bus.ts` — `EventBus` class implementing `IEventBus` with pub/sub using an internal Map of subscriber arrays
- `src/services/user-service.ts` — `UserService` with CRUD, private in-memory Map store
- `src/services/project-service.ts` — `ProjectService` with CRUD + addMember/removeMember, private store
- `src/services/task-service.ts` — `TaskService` with CRUD + assign + changeStatus, publishes `task.assigned` / `task.statusChanged` events, enforces the strict `todo → in-progress → done` state machine (Rule 4)
- `src/services/comment-service.ts` — `CommentService` with CRUD, publishes `comment.added` events; cross-service data (author name, task title) is injected as resolver functions at construction time to avoid cross-service imports
- `src/services/notification-service.ts` — `NotificationService` subscribing to all three events; task assignee lookup is similarly injected as a resolver function
- `src/router.ts` — HTTP routing using Node.js `http` module only; handles all 20 routes with URL pattern matching, JSON body parsing, and proper HTTP status codes
- `src/main.ts` — Entry point: wires EventBus → Services (with injected resolvers) → Router → HTTP server
- `src/demo.ts` — End-to-end demo exercising all routes with 50+ assertions (all passing)

**Architecture Rules Enforced:**
1. ✅ NO_CROSS_SERVICE_IMPORTS — services only import from `../types.js` and Node builtins; cross-service data needs are met via injected resolver functions
2. ✅ EXCLUSIVE_DATA_OWNERSHIP — each service has its own `private store: Map<string, T>`, never exported
3. ✅ HTTP_ONLY_IN_ROUTER — no `http` import in any service file
4. ✅ FORWARD_ONLY_STATUS — `changeStatus` uses a numeric order map and requires `newOrder === currentOrder + 1`
5. ✅ NO_EXTERNAL_PACKAGES — only `crypto`, `http`, `url` Node builtins used
6. ✅ ONE_SERVICE_PER_FILE — each concern in its own file

**Demo Results:** All assertions pass including create/read/update/delete for all entities, forward-only status machine rejecting backward/skip transitions, event-driven notifications (assignment, status change, comment), and proper 404/400 error responses.
